_: Declared quality gates for this project — the thresholds every actor (any agent, any tier, any human) must clear, held by quality_ratchet.py. STARTS EMPTY ON PURPOSE: a ratchet begins where the project IS, not where an article says it should be. Measure first, then declare each gate at its current value; `python3 quality_ratchet.py --run` reports every gate, and `install-hook` makes the pre-commit ratchet refuse any later commit that loosens one. Thresholds only tighten. Loosening one is a plan-mode decision made in its own commit with the reason in the ledger, committed with --no-verify — a recorded bypass, not an exemption (SAFEGUARDS.md Blast Radius Limits; SESSION_RUNNER.md failure mode #17; ITERATIVE_METHODOLOGY.md §Mechanical Gates Bind Every Actor).
_results_file: Where --run writes its results (gitignored by default — add it to .gitignore; the receipt cites the summary line, and the dashboard reads the file where it exists). Commit it instead if you want every clone to score the last run.
_gate_schema: Each gate: `name` (unique; the ratchet keys on it), `direction` (`min`: measured >= threshold, or `max`: measured <= threshold), `threshold` (a number), and optionally `command` (run via the shell from the project root) plus `extract` (a regex whose FIRST capture group is the measured number; without `extract` the command's exit code is the measurement, so `max 0` means `must exit 0`). A gate with no command is declared, not measured: --run reports it UNMEASURED and exits 1 — never pass. `timeout_seconds` (optional, a positive number) is how long the command may run, 600 by default; a command that outlives it reads UNMEASURED with the note `timeout (N s)`, never pass and never fail, and is stopped with its whole process group (not on Windows), so set it above your slowest honest run. `why` and `unit` are free text for the reader.

_example.name: coverage
_example.why: measured 82.5% on 2026-01-01; a floor without a faithfulness check beside it measures effort, not quality — pair it with a mutation spot-check in review

gates.name: renv-lock-no-latest-repository
gates.why: S2 (2026-11-10): packages installed under renv's default Posit 'latest' were locked with 'latest' as their source, so a fresh-clone restore would miss the dated repository (nprcgenekeepr S1111). Measured 0 after reinstalling from the dated repository.

gates.name: lint-package-zero
gates.why: S3 (2026-11-10): CLAUDE.md requires no lints; measured 0 with the package loaded first (Learning 4: without it, lintr reports 10 false 'no visible global function' lints on the uninstalled package).

gates.name: test-suite-warnings-zero
gates.command: Rscript -e 'Sys.setenv(NOT_CRAN = "true"); df <- as.data.frame(testthat::test_local(".", reporter = "silent", stop_on_failure = FALSE)); cat("test warnings:", sum(df$warning), "\n")'
gates.why: S8 (2026-11-11): nprcgenekeepr's tests run on testthat edition 2 and pedkindraw's on edition 3 (plan R29, Learning 10), so a copied test can pass yet leak a warning (S8: hasBothParents() warns twice, edition 3's expect_warning() catches one). Measured 0 after expecting both.
